cue: Out-of-focus things smear up and down. Tap the screen to move the focus.

DEUTAN.note: Vienot, Brettel and Mollon 1999, entered from memory

rows: Cats see about a fifth to a tenth as much detail as people do. This view is blurred to match.
Cats have two kinds of colour-sensing cells in their eyes, where people have three. Reds and greens are hard for them to tell apart, so reds look olive or grey to a cat.
A cat’s pupil closes to a narrow vertical slit, a shape common in animals that hunt by ambush. A slit like this smears out-of-focus things up and down, and this view does the same.
A cat takes in about 200 degrees around itself, and a person about 180. A phone camera sees far less than either, so this view bends the picture at its edges to suggest the wider sweep.
Cats can see in light six to eight times dimmer than people need. This view brightens the shadows to show it.
A phone camera can’t measure distance, so this view assumes that things lower in the picture are closer. Tap the screen to move the focus.
This view assumes that a cat sees most sharply straight ahead.
